newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end more than one percent down.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end more than one percent down.

text.p: Italian stocks fell more than one percent in subdued trade on Monday but ended above the day's lows with turnover reaching just over 800 billion lire ($478 million) on the cash market.

Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) ended 3.8 percent up at 3,578 lire per ordinary share, in contrast to the rest of the market. Dealers attributed the gain to renewed expectations of acquisitions and on 1996 results expected to be released towards the end of the month.
The blue chip Mib30 index ended 1.26 percent off at 18,404 while the all-share Mibtel index was 1.22 percent down at 12,361.
Other banks trailed BCI, with Ambroveneto ending 1.99 percent higher at 4,397 lire while San Paolo bankgin group was 1.23 percent firmer at 11,551.

Telecom stocks ended mostly down with state telecoms holding Stet 3.2 percent weaker at 8172 and state telecoms operator Telecom Italia 2.82 percent down at 4,415 lire, maintaining the 1.8 ratio on the two groups' shares ahead of their merger.

Among industrials, carmaker Fiat was down 1.69 percent at 5,190 almost in line with the market while agri industrial group Montedison and tyre and cable maker Pirelli were just over two percent weaker.
